statement.p: Compute the line integral of the scalar function f(x,y,z)= 2x^2+8z

static.solution:
[Step 1.] Compute \| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\|.
{\mathbf{c}}'(t)= \frac{\,d}{\,dt}\left\lt e^t , t^2,t \right> = \left\lt e^t ,2t,1 \right> \quad\Rightarrow\quad \| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| =\sqrt{e^{2t}+4 t^2+1} [Step 2.] Write out f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right).
We substitute x= e^t, y= t^2, z=t in f( x,y,z )=2 x^2+8z to obtain: f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)=2 e^{2t}+8t [Step 3.] Compute the line integral.
We have \int_{\mathcal{C}} f( x,y,z ) \,ds =\int_0^{8} f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| \,dt = \int_0^{8} (2 e^{2t}+8t)\sqrt{e^{2t}+4 t^2+1} \,dt We compute the integral using the substitution u={e^{2t}+4 t^2+1}, du=\left({2 e^{2t}+8t}\right) \,dt. We get: \int_{\mathcal{C}} f( x,y,z ) \,ds = \int_2^{e^{16}+257} u^{1/2} \,du= \frac23 u^{3/2}\bigg|_2^{e^{16}+257}= \frac23\left({(e^{16}+257)}^{3/2}-2^{3/2}\right)
